name: Cape Henlopen
pitch: For the water bottle that keeps ending up at Cape Henlopen.
about: Cape Henlopen sits where Delaware Bay meets the Atlantic outside Lewes. Beaches, dunes, bike trails, fishing and camping, and the busiest state park in Delaware.
art: Dune line, Harbor of Refuge light, horseshoe crab, coastal grass. Pick two — not all four.

name: Rehoboth Beach
pitch: A small mark for the beach that keeps making the weekend plan.
about: Rehoboth is Delaware's best-known beach town — boardwalk, bandstand, and the one whose dog dates moved in 2026.
art: One recognizable cue only: bandstand silhouette OR boardwalk line OR umbrella row. Generic beach art could be any coastal town and is worth nothing.

name: Indian River Inlet
pitch: You know the bridge before you see the sign.
about: The inlet cuts Delaware Seashore State Park in two, under the Charles W. Cullen Bridge. Surf fishing, surfing, camping and the strongest current on the Delaware coast.
art: The bridge is the whole design. Cable-stay silhouette, inlet current line, maybe a surf rod. Named for the inlet rather than the park because that's what people picture.

name: Bethany Beach
pitch: Same week, same stretch of sand, every year.
about: The quiet end of the Delaware beaches, and the one families come back to for the same week every summer. Dogs are off the beach two weeks longer than Rehoboth.
art: Boardwalk and ocean, or beach-chair silhouettes. Check the totem pole's status before using it — it is a specific commissioned artwork, not a generic town motif.

name: Dewey Beach
pitch: Ocean on one side, bay on the other, a mile between them.
about: A mile of sand between the Atlantic and Rehoboth Bay. The only Delaware beach town that never closes to dogs — though it does require its own license.
art: The bay/ocean duality is the idea: two water lines, one strip of town between. Sunrise and sunset on the same sticker.

name: Lewes
pitch: Keep a little Lewes on the water bottle.
about: The first town in the first state, on the canal where the ferry comes in. Historic front street on one side, Cape Henlopen on the other.
art: Canal and front-street rooflines, or the ferry. 'Delaware' belongs in the product title — there is a Lewes in England and a Lewes in Sussex County, and search can't tell.

name: White Clay Creek
pitch: Not a beach. Still one of your places.
about: A wild valley on the Pennsylvania line above Newark — trails, the creek itself, and the disc golf course. The test of whether inland Delaware carries the same attachment as the coast.
art: Creek, sycamore, stone bridge. Deliberately not coastal — this design exists to find out whether the identity works away from sand.

name: Dewey Beach — The Dog Goes Too
pitch: One of the few Delaware beaches where the dog still gets the sand in July.
about: Dewey allows dogs year-round, on a town license, with limited hours in summer. NO DATES OR HOURS GO ON THIS STICKER — they change, and a sticker cannot be corrected.
art: Dewey's bay/ocean line with a dog silhouette. The dog variant of 005, not a separate town.
